This integration is called a provirus and can remain inactive in the human DNA without causing any damage or changes to the genetic material. However, in rare cases, a virus can integrate into the wrong place in the human DNA and cause a genetic mutation. This is extremely rare and is not a common form of viral infection. In summary, although viruses can integrate their genetic material into human DNA, it is not common for them to directly modify human DNA.
